meta.about: The set-up flow from the home screen to the briefing, its 3D stage, the new inputs (in play and in the menus), the weapon wheel, the four-slot weapon bar and the saved set-up (docs/unreal/LOADOUT.md sections 2, 4 and 7). Strings are in frontend_text.json; the screens name their keys.
meta.units: seconds, degrees, centimetres (Unreal units: this file has no web source)

parity.about: The set-up that must play exactly as the web game (LOADOUT.md 1.2). It is also the set-up of a first start, and what any invalid saved set-up falls back to.

carry.note: contiguous: carried guns fill slots 1..n with no gap; removing a gun closes the gap

same.note: starts at once with the remembered set-up (or the parity set-up the first time); Enter and gamepad Start do the same, as the web title's Enter and Start did

transitions.about: Every edge of the diagram in LOADOUT.md 2.1. `remember` writes the set-up to the save game when the edge is taken.
edges: first frame of the title state
Same set-up, Enter, gamepad Start; remember
Next (at least one gun carried); remember
Change on a line of the summary
Change set-up on the death or debrief card (the run ends as Back to title does, then the Loadout screen opens)

stage.about: The 3D set behind the set-up screens (LOADOUT.md 2.11): a closed room spawned at run time high above the block, so the block's fog, sky light and sun do not reach it. Every value is a placeholder for the art pass.

room.note: a cyclorama room; engine cube walls until the art exists (status missing)

bench.note: a steel workbench top under the turntable; status missing

turntable.note: spin: degrees per second when untouched for idleAfter s; drag: degrees per mouse pixel; stick: degrees per second at full right stick; snap: seconds an attachment takes to slide into its socket

arms.note: the crew member's arms in first-person framing playing the Inspect clip with the first carried gun; drag orbits up to 35 degrees

focus.note: offsets in centimetres in the gun's frame (X along the bore) from the turntable centre; the camera eases there in 0.4 s when a slot tab is chosen

cameras.title: the title fly-through (spec 04 3.4), kept running behind Home, Level and Game style
cameras.firstPerson: the player's own camera at the level's playerStart, the arms holding the first carried gun: the intro starts from this view

input.about: Mappings added on top of config.json player.keys / mouseButtons / padButtons (which come from the web game and are not edited). In the parity set-up none of them changes a rule unless pressed.

game.note: replaces the web 'swap' meaning of the wheel and D-pad up: the next carried gun. With two guns next = previous = the other gun, which is what swap did
as next, backwards; the wheel keeps config player.input.wheelDebounce (0.28 s)
unchanged key, new meaning: the last gun used (quick swap); with two guns that is the other one. Held for wheelHold it opens the weapon wheel
pad: a tap of View (Back); held for inspectHold it inspects instead

input.magazineCheck: Reload (R, X) with a full magazine, or with an empty reserve, plays the magazine check: the rules refuse the reload as they always did, so nothing else happens

menu.about: Per screen: mouse, keyboard and gamepad. Common to all: Back = B, Esc, the back button or right-click on empty space; accept = A, Enter, Space, left click; Next = Start, Enter on the Next button or the Next button; the D-pad and left stick move the focus with config player.input.pad.nav (0.6, 0.38 s, 0.17 s).

crew.mouse: click a card to choose; drag the stage to orbit; Next
crew.keys: Left / Right choose; Enter next; Esc back
crew.pad: D-pad or stick left / right choose; A next; right stick orbits; B back

loadout.mouse: click a roster card: carry it in the first empty slot, or in the selected slot when all four are full; drag a card onto a slot to put it there; drag a slot onto another to swap their order; right-click a slot to empty it; the wrench on a card or a slot (or double-click) opens the workbench; drag the stage to turn the gun, wheel zooms
loadout.keys: arrows move the focus over the class tabs, the roster grid and the slots; Enter carries the focused roster gun (or selects the focused slot); 1 to 4 put the focused roster gun in that slot; Shift + Up / Down move the focused slot; Delete empties it; Space opens the workbench for the focused gun; Tab jumps between the roster and the slots; Esc back
loadout.pad: D-pad / stick move the focus; A carries the focused roster gun or selects a slot; X empties the focused slot; LB / RB move the focused slot up / down; Y opens the workbench; LT / RT zoom; right stick turns the gun; Start next; B back

workbench.mouse: click a slot tab, then an option; the arrows beside the gun's name (or the carried-gun strip) change gun; Reset build; drag turns, wheel zooms
workbench.keys: Left / Right slot tab; Up / Down option; Enter fit; Backspace factory part; Q / E previous / next carried gun; R reset build; Esc done
workbench.pad: D-pad left / right slot tab; up / down option; A fit; X factory part; LB / RB previous / next carried gun; Y reset build; right stick turns; LT / RT zoom; B done

level.mouse: click a level card; click Day or Night; Next
level.keys: Left / Right level; Up / Down to the time picker, Left / Right time; Enter next
level.pad: D-pad left / right level; up / down to the time picker; A next

style.mouse: click Story or Hold the Block; click a difficulty; Next
style.keys: Left / Right mode; Down to the difficulty, Left / Right; Enter next
style.pad: D-pad left / right mode; down to the difficulty; A next

briefing.mouse: Hit the block; Change beside a line jumps to that screen
briefing.keys: Enter hits the block; Up / Down to a Change link; Esc back
briefing.pad: A or Start hits the block; D-pad to a Change link; B back

wheel.about: The weapon wheel (LOADOUT.md 4.6): hold Q or Y. The quick swap the press started goes on; the wheel only redirects it, through the rules' own switch reversal.
wheel.note: deadzone: share of the stick or of mouseRadius (pixels of mouse travel since the wheel opened) below which nothing is selected; releasing then keeps the quick swap's target. timeScale 1: the game does not slow down

weaponBar.slots: one per carried gun (two in the parity set-up: the web bar exactly), then the melee slot
weaponBar.fireModeTag: AUTO or SEMI under the count of a gun that has both modes
weaponBar.attachmentPips: one small icon per fitted non-baseline attachment, under the gun's silhouette

save.about: The remembered set-up (LOADOUT.md 7), a block of the one save game that also holds the nine settings and the best Hold the Block score (ARCHITECTURE 2.2 Core/Settings/MISaveGame). Mode, difficulty and time stay the existing settings keys and are not copied here.

fields.guns: array of up to 4 names (guns.json ids), slot order
fields.builds: map gun id -> map slot id -> attachment id or None; kept for every gun ever built, carried or not, so a gun put back on keeps its build
fields.fireModes: map gun id -> auto | semi: the mode the gun starts the next run in (the last one used)
fields.seen: array of names: guns, attachments, crew and levels the player has looked at (the NEW badge)
fields.played: bool: at least one run started (the Same set-up button shows the remembered set-up, else the parity set-up)

validation: an unknown crew, level or gun id is dropped (a gun pack removed): crew -> rule, level -> block, guns -> the remaining ones, and the parity guns when none remains
an attachment not in the gun's compatibility options is dropped (the slot falls back to its default)
a required slot without a valid choice takes its default
duplicates and gaps in guns are removed; more than carry.max are cut
a mode the level does not provide falls back to the first mode it does provide
